findings.title: Spawned workers do not pass the Process type check
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose instances are SpawnProcess objects, not instances of the separate multiprocessing.Process class. This check therefore skips kill() for every production worker. When a worker is considered hung, its replacement is started while the original remains alive and is removed from self.processes. If the original resumes, both workers can flush the same shards, and the original can no longer be supervised. The same incorrect check at line 346 also skips termination during shutdown. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the actual spawn-context process class instead.

findings.title: Shutdown abandons remaining workers when the deadline expires
findings.body: When the shared join deadline expires, this loop breaks without terminating any of the remaining workers. Those workers may still be blocked in Redis or Kafka operations despite the stopped flag. During a rebalance the consumer can subsequently create a new flusher for those shards while the old workers remain alive and unsupervised. Deadline expiry should stop waiting, but should still terminate and clean up every outstanding worker.

findings.title: The added wait is patched into a no-op
findings.body: test_basic replaces time.sleep with a no-op at line 15, so this time.sleep(0.1) does not give the background flusher time to observe the updated drift. step.join() then sets the stop flag, allowing the worker to exit before flushing the span and leaving messages empty. The test remains scheduling-dependent rather than reliably testing flushing. Use an unpatched sleep or, preferably, wait for an explicit indication that the output has been produced before joining.
